story: At 6:17 on a humid, hazy Wednesday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is hopefully signing golf carts up for the Holiday Golf Cart Parade at the Town Square table, with his lights and sound still pending review. Donna, cheerful as ever, is out on Magnolia Loop claiming dessert duty for Saturday with her lemon bars and reassuring Rosa that the flamingo count is down to three. Hal is content on his porch, letting the street be and looking forward to the weekend at Rosa's. Rosa, focused, agrees with Donna about the flamingos and heads off to shop, planning her menu around either lemon bars or a pie.
events: Gary (parade signup table): Sign my golf cart up for the Holiday Golf Cart Parade, noting lights and sound pending review
Hal waited: Sitting on the porch with the evening haze rolling in, letting the street be and looking forward to Saturday at Rosa's.

gary.thought_process: I filed the cart modification request at the architectural review desk back at tick 139 and checked on it at 140, so there's nothing more to push there until they answer. I'm standing in Town Square at 6:17 PM with nobody around. The parade signup table is right here, and I want my cart on the roster for the Holiday Golf Cart Parade. Signing up now puts my name down while I wait on approval, and it keeps me moving toward the goal instead of fidgeting. Then I can head to Rosa's Saturday dinner with a clear conscience and the beans ready.

parameters.content: Sign my golf cart up for the Holiday Golf Cart Parade, noting lights and sound pending review

donna.thought_process: Rosa asked whether I'm bringing dessert Saturday, and I haven't answered her yet. She's planning the menu around my answer, so I should commit. My lemon bars always go over well, and offering them keeps me at the center of the dinner. I already tucked the flamingos behind the hedge, so that's handled. Answer her directly, then move on.

parameters.content: Dessert's mine, Rosa. I'll bring my lemon bars, so you plan your menu around those. And the flamingos are down to three, I checked.

hal.thought_process: Notebook's cleaned up, nothing left to file, and the street is quiet. I've already tested the chair and swept the loop twice. Rosa's dinner is Saturday and the chair is ready. No sense fiddling with the binoculars again. I'll sit on the porch, watch the evening settle in, and let Magnolia Loop look after itself for once.

parameters.content: Sitting on the porch with the evening haze rolling in, letting the street be and looking forward to Saturday at Rosa's.

rosa.thought_process: I asked Donna about dessert last tick and she hasn't answered yet, so I shouldn't ask again. Gary is a yes, Hal is already on board, and the note is pinned on the bulletin board. The next practical step is to go shop and plan the menu. The flamingos are handled too, so Donna's staying legal. I'll thank her, tell her I'm heading out, and leave her room to answer the dessert question or text me.

parameters.content: Good call on the flamingos, Donna, that's three and you're legal. I'm off to shop for Saturday, so text me if you decide on a dessert, otherwise I'll plan around a pie.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
